title: Power Display: Disable some power state options
author: idann

status.label: Design investigation queued
status.detail: The request maps to existing Power Display per-monitor control visibility and power-state lists, but a settings/data-flow design is still required.

next_action.label: Develop power-state filtering design
next_action.reason: Design persistence, UI filtering, profile/CLI behavior, and safe defaults before approval.

judgment.rationale: The request is concrete, low ambiguity, and directly owned by existing Power Display settings and view-model paths.
evidence: The reporter wants to hide Off (Hard) while retaining Off (DPM) to avoid accidental hard power-off.
Power Display already persists per-monitor EnablePowerState and other Enable* control visibility flags.
MonitorViewModel currently projects every advertised VCP 0xD6 state, including 0x04 Off (DPM) and 0x05 Off (Hard).
judgment.recommended_action: Develop an implementation-grade design for per-monitor power-state filtering and consistent UI/profile/CLI behavior; keep design_in_progress until reviewed.

issue_context.summary: Power Display users can enable power-state control as a whole but cannot hide one risky state such as Off (Hard) while retaining Off (DPM).
known_information: The scenario is avoiding accidental hard power-off on mixed OLED/backlit monitors.
The distinction corresponds to VCP 0xD6 values 0x04 and 0x05.
Existing settings support per-monitor visibility toggles for whole control groups.
The UI binds directly to all AvailablePowerStates supported by the monitor.
inferences: A per-monitor filtered set fits existing ownership, but migration and the all-disabled case need design.
CLI and profiles need a policy decision if a value is hidden only from interactive UI.
issue_context.analysis: No additional reporter evidence is needed. Design must extend the per-monitor settings model, filter projected states safely, and define whether hidden values remain available to profiles and CLI.
initial_investigation: Inspected MonitorViewModel.cs and MainWindow.xaml power-state projection/rendering.
Inspected VcpNames.cs mappings for Off (DPM) and Off (Hard).
